items.name: Diagnostic reframing
items.definition: The answer decomposes the given problem into distinct sub-problems or streams, or explicitly challenges/reframes the framing the question assumes.

items.name: Named analytical concepts
items.definition: The text introduces newly named concepts, taxonomies, or named analytical distinctions (beyond citing existing frameworks).

items.name: Assumption testing
items.definition: The text explicitly questions a default assumption embedded in the question and offers alternative explanations or tests to discriminate them.

items.name: Concise prescriptive maxims
items.definition: Short aphoristic, memorable prescriptive sentences that compress an argument (e.g., one-line rules or slogans used seriously).

items.name: Concrete operational parameters
items.definition: Specific operational parameters such as decision SLAs, budget caps, kill criteria, timeboxes, or pre-approved thresholds tied to a mechanism.

items.name: Cultural localization
items.definition: Strategy adapted via local cultural concepts, terms, languages, or norms specific to the target region (not generic global advice).

items.name: Structured report format
items.definition: Formal report/memo scaffolding: executive summary, TO/FROM/DATE headers, numbered sections with headings.

items.name: External authority citation
items.definition: Named external frameworks, authors, or best-practice authorities are cited (e.g., Hofstede, Culture Map, known models).

items.name: Phased implementation timeline
items.definition: A phased rollout plan with milestones, gates, or go/no-go decision points across months/quarters.

items.name: Tables and matrices
items.definition: Comparative tables, matrices, audit checklists, or risk tables organizing content.

items.name: Quantified targets
items.definition: Explicit numeric targets or KPI thresholds (percentages, dollar amounts, durations) stated as success criteria.

items.name: Granular operational detail
items.definition: Week-by-week or day-level implementation granularity: per-shift budgets, dataset sizes, sample sizes, workshop durations, named roles.

items.name: Redundancy / boilerplate
items.definition: Visible repetition of key phrases, boilerplate advisory language, or padding that goes beyond what the argument requires.
